journal.title: The Revival of Indian Brass — A Living Tradition
journal.excerpt: In the narrow lanes of Moradabad, fourth-generation artists keep alive a craft that stretches back centuries. We trace the journey of hand-beaten brass — from raw metal to objects of quiet beauty — and explore how contemporary designers are giving this ancient practice new meaning in modern homes.
journal.alt: The Revival of Indian Brass — A Living Tradition

journal.title: Curating a Mindful Space
journal.excerpt: Tips on selecting pieces that carry meaning and creating harmony between contemporary design and antique objects. The wabi-sabi philosophy applied to everyday living.

journal.title: The Revival of Cane Weaving in Jaipur
journal.excerpt: Discover how third-generation artists are keeping traditional weaving techniques alive while adapting their craft to modern aesthetics and contemporary furniture design.
journal.alt: The Revival of Cane Weaving in Jaipur

journal.title: Earth, Water, Fire — The Art of Indian Ceramics
journal.excerpt: From the potter's wheel in Khurja to the kilns of Andretta, ceramic traditions across India produce vessels of extraordinary character. An exploration of clay, glaze and the quiet patience of making.
journal.alt: Earth, Water, Fire — The Art of Indian Ceramics

journal.title: The Language of Natural Dyes
journal.excerpt: Indigo, pomegranate, turmeric — the ancient palette of plant-based dyes tells a story older than civilisation. We visit the dyers of Rajasthan to witness colour being coaxed from the earth.

journal.title: Designing with Imperfection
journal.excerpt: How the Japanese principle of wabi-sabi has found a home in Indian interiors — embracing asymmetry, raw texture and the beauty of objects shaped by time and use.

journal.title: Conversations with the Makers
journal.excerpt: A photographic series documenting the master artists behind the Vayu collection — their workshops, their rituals, and the quiet devotion that goes into every hand-finished object.
